scope: Document management: list search and sort, rename, delete to the trash, and restore, over HTTP, the CLI, and the web page. Storage and document management only; no chemistry or external formats.
environment: Linux 6.6 (WSL2), Rust 1.95.0, Node 22.22.2; browser checks with Chromium 141.0.7390.37 (Playwright build v1194) via playwright-core 1.56.1
design: The Application filters (title contains the query, ignoring case) and sorts (title, or last commit by the stored file's modification time); the web page and the CLI only pass the query. Rename commits the new title as one revision through the ordinary save path, only for a copy without unsaved changes and without an abandoned draft. Delete moves documents/<id>.json to trash/<id>.json with one rename, after checking the base revision and the absence of drafts under the document's save lock and its draft owner lock; restore moves it back under the save lock. While a rename or delete commits, the session is held and edits to it are answered busy. Rename, delete, and restore follow the request order of #19: the request_id is marked running (a repeat is answered request_in_progress at once), a finished reply is looked up without waiting, then the document's turn is taken (at most 3 s, else busy). A rename's reply is remembered with the session, delete and restore replies per process. Trash and restore writes report permission errors as Denied (reason read_only). The web client asks about a lost rename, delete, or restore reply once more with the same request_id and polls while it is in progress; a later attempt is a new request that the operation's precondition refuses if the first took effect.

New in this change: the_list_is_searched_by_title_and_sorted_by_title_or_last_save, renaming_commits_at_once_and_needs_a_clean_copy, renaming_or_deleting_waits_for_an_earlier_sessions_draft, deleting_moves_a_clean_document_to_the_trash_and_restoring_brings_it_back, deleting_refuses_to_lose_unsaved_work_anywhere, copies_in_other_processes_never_bring_a_deleted_document_back, edits_wait_while_a_delete_is_in_progress, renames_and_deletes_queued_behind_a_stalled_save_are_answered_busy_without_changes, a_delete_or_restore_asked_about_while_it_writes_is_answered_at_once_and_not_repeated, a_rename_asked_about_while_it_commits_is_answered_at_once, rename_delete_and_restore_failures_say_whether_retrying_can_help; file store: trashing_moves_the_document_whole_and_restoring_brings_it_back, trashing_is_refused_while_another_writer_or_a_draft_holds_the_document, a_trash_move_or_restore_refused_by_permissions_is_denied_and_moves_nothing.

The list step and the contract smoke make the listed documents an hour old before the rename, so the recency order they check does not depend on the wall clock between two writes (see limits). limits: Nothing is ever removed from the trash: there is no permanent delete or emptying yet, and trashed documents keep their space.
Another process's unsaved work that has no draft yet is invisible to the CLI; deleting the document then succeeds, and that work is kept only through save as copy.

Sort recent uses the stored file's modification time, a wall-clock time. A clock adjustment can reorder documents saved within it: on WSL2 the clock stepped back about 0.7 s between two writes in 2 of 8 local browser runs and in 2 of 120 direct API probes, listing the earlier save first. Another program touching the file also changes it.
Listing restores and validates every stored and trashed document; a large library lists slowly (outside the session lock).

A rename, delete, or restore whose reply stays lost beyond one re-ask and the in-progress polling is reported as failed; trying again is safe but may meet its own first attempt as revision_conflict or document_not_found.
